spans.s: + छेद भक्ति- + छेद, m. certain streaks on the forehead, nose, cheeks, breast, and arms, which denote a follower of Viṣṇu.
+ दास भक्त- + दास (vb. [] भज्), m. a slave maintained in consideration of service,

भक्त, i. e. ptcple. pf. pass. of भज् (in the signification To cook, cf. also भक्ष्), n.
 1. Food,

भक्ति, i. e. भज् and भञ्ज् + ति,
 1. Worship, Vikr. d. 1; service.
 2. Devotion, Hit. iii. d. 65.
 3. Attachment, Pañc. i. d. 326.
 4. Faith, Pañc. 71, 4; belief, Śāṇḍilyas. ed. Ballantyne, 76 sqq.
 5. Fracture, breaking,
भक्तिभाज्, i. e. भक्ति-भज्, adj. Devout, Pañc. 236, 20.
भक्ति + मन्त्, adj., f. ती, Devoted, faithful, Pañc. pr. d. 5.

भक्ष्, akin to भज् and भञ्ज्, i. 1, Par. Ātm., and i. 10, Par. (in epic poetry also Ātm.),
 1. To devour,

. To enjoy, Pañc. 137, 20.
 4. To bite, Pañc. 62, 23;

.
 --Ptcple. of the fut. pass. भक्ष्य, Eatable, allowed to be eaten,

.
 --Cf. ϕαγεῖν, perhaps ϕακός, ϕάσηλος; Lat. fames, perhaps bacca.

भक्ष् + अ,
 I. m., f. षा, and n. (Pañc. rec. orn.), Eating food, Pañc. 53, 23.
 II. latter part of comp. adj. Devouring,

. A feeder, Hit. i. d. 54, M.M.
 II. f. षिका, A meal.

भक्षण, i. e. भक्ष् + अन, n.
 1. Eating, Pañc. 114, 10; being eaten, 88, 25.
 2. Enjoying, Vedāntas. in
-भक्ष् + इन्, adj. Eating; in सर्व-, adj. Eating all kinds of food, Pañc. i. d. 472.
+ योग भक्ति- + योग, m. devotion, as shown by implicit faith in any divinity.
+ स्थान भक्ष- + स्थान, n. state of being (one's) food, Pañc. 131, 2 (भक्षस्थाने स्थितम् अपि, although you are destined to be his food).
